questions.q:
The atomic clock on ISRO's IRNSS-1F stopped working in March 2026, weakening NavIC. Consider the following statements:
1. NavIC is an independent regional navigation system developed by ISRO, covering the region up to about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass.
2. NVS-02, launched in January 2025, failed to reach its final orbit.
3. NavIC was approved after the US denied GPS data to India during the 1999 Kargil conflict.
4. NavIC's Standard Positioning Service uses only the L1 band.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Standard Positioning Service uses the L5 and S bands, with accuracy better than 20 metres; L1 signals were added only with the second-generation NVS satellites. At least four satellites with working atomic clocks are needed, and six of eleven NavIC satellites have lost clocks.
questions.h: NavIC SPS: L5 and S bands.

questions.q:
The European Space Agency lost contact with one of the two spacecraft of its Proba-3 mission. Consider the following statements:
1. Proba-3 is ESA's first precision formation-flying mission.
2. Its two spacecraft, a Coronagraph and an Occulter, fly about 150 metres apart to create artificial solar eclipses.
3. Proba-3 is a joint NASA-ISRO mission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Proba-3 is a European mission; by blocking the Sun's disc with the Occulter, the Coronagraph can image the solar corona for long periods.

questions.q:
A new study on NASA's DART mission was reported in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. DART struck Didymos, the larger body of the asteroid pair, on 26 September 2022.
2. The mission shortened the orbit of the moonlet Dimorphos by about 33 minutes.
3. The new study found that the orbit of the whole Didymos pair around the Sun changed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DART hit Dimorphos, the moonlet, not Didymos itself. It was the first demonstration of asteroid deflection by kinetic impact, and the study widened the effect to the whole pair's solar orbit.

questions.q:
Astronomers using the MeerKAT telescope found the brightest and most distant megamaser known. Consider the following statements:
1. MeerKAT is located in Australia and is a precursor to the Square Kilometre Array.
2. A megamaser is a giant beam of microwaves emitted when two galaxies merge, compressing gas clouds and exciting hydroxyl molecules.
3. Masers amplify microwaves, whereas lasers amplify visible light.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MeerKAT is in South Africa, so statement 1 is wrong, although it is a precursor to the Square Kilometre Array. Megamasers act as cosmic signposts that reveal details of galaxies in the early universe.

questions.q:
The LHCb experiment at CERN announced the discovery of the Xi-cc-plus. Consider the following statements:
1. It is a baryon made of two charm quarks and one down quark.
2. It is about four times heavier than a proton.
3. It is a meson made of a quark and an antiquark.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Baryons contain three quarks, mesons two. It is only the second baryon seen with two heavy quarks, after the Xi-cc-plus-plus of 2017, and helps study the strong force.

questions.q:
The Department of Science and Technology approved 23 institutions to set up quantum teaching labs under the National Quantum Mission (NQM). Consider the following statements:
1. The NQM has an outlay of Rs 6,003 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31.
2. Its domains are quantum computing, communication, sensing and metrology, and materials and devices.
3. The mission is run by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
4. More than 100 other proposals are under evaluation.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NQM is under the Department of Science and Technology, not MeitY.

questions.q:
Visakhapatnam was selected to host a high-energy proton accelerator for India's three-stage nuclear programme. Consider the following statements:
1. It will be developed by the Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology, Indore.
2. RRCAT developed the Indus-1 and Indus-2 synchrotron sources.
3. Accelerator-Driven Systems use neutrons to convert fissile U-233 into thorium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ADS neutrons convert fertile thorium into fissile U-233, not the reverse; this supports the thorium stage of the programme.

questions.q: The LIGO-India gravitational-wave observatory, expected by 2030 after delays, is being built at
questions.e: LIGO-India would be the fifth node of the global network alongside Hanford and Livingston (US), Virgo (Italy) and KAGRA (Japan). It is led by DAE and DST with IUCAA Pune as partner.

questions.q:
A pilot plant for Nd-Fe-B rare-earth permanent magnets was set up at ARCI, Hyderabad, and the Ministry of Heavy Industries invited bids for a sintered REPM scheme. Consider the following statements:
1. The scheme targets 6,000 MTPA of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity.
2. Five beneficiaries will each get up to 1,200 MTPA.
3. Its outlay of Rs 7,280 crore is mostly capital subsidy, with a Rs 750 crore sales-linked incentive.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Capital subsidy is Rs 750 crore and sales-linked incentive Rs 6,450 crore, so statement 3 reverses the split. REPMs are used in EVs, wind turbines, electronics and defence.

questions.q:
The Prime Minister launched a nationwide HPV vaccination campaign for 14-year-old girls. Consider the following statements:
1. The campaign provides the vaccine free at government health facilities.
2. India's national programme uses the quadrivalent Gardasil-4, which targets types 6, 11, 16 and 18.
3. Cervavac, made by the Serum Institute of India, is an indigenously developed vaccine against the same four strains.
4. India's programme relies on a nonavalent vaccine.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The national programme uses the quadrivalent Gardasil-4. Types 16 and 18 cause about 70 per cent of cervical cancers globally and over 80 per cent in India. The drive is voluntary, with parental consent, and supports the WHO 90-70-90 targets by 2030.

questions.q:
India's largest pregnancy cohort study, GARBH-INi, aims to develop indigenous AI-driven solutions for preterm births. Consider the following statements:
1. The cohort covers 12,000 women and is led by THSTI, Faridabad.
2. It is supported by the Indian Council of Medical Research.
3. It forms part of the Atal Jai Anusandhan Biotech Mission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GARBH-INi is supported by the Department of Biotechnology, not ICMR. It runs a national biorepository and the GARBH-INi-DRISHTI data-sharing platform.

questions.q: CALM-Brain was launched in Bengaluru in March 2026 by the Rohini Nilekani Centre for Brain and Mind of NIMHANS and NCBS-TIFR. It is India's first
o: digital open-source repository of brain data on major psychiatric disorders
AI chatbot for school mental health
questions.e: It covers addiction, bipolar disorder, dementia, OCD and schizophrenia, over 2,000 individuals across 900 families, and is linked to a stem-cell biobank. DBT and the Pratiksha Trust funded it.

questions.q:
The Centre temporarily discontinued fortified rice under PMGKAY after an IIT Kharagpur study. Consider the following statements:
1. The study found micronutrient levels fall under typical storage conditions.
2. Fortified rice kernels contain iron, folic acid and vitamin B12.
3. Bio-fortification means adding micronutrients to food during processing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bio-fortification improves nutrient content while the crop grows (through breeding), whereas adding micronutrients during processing is industrial fortification. Rice in the central pool is often stored for 2 to 3 years.

questions.q:
The World Obesity Atlas 2026 was released on World Obesity Day (4 March). Consider the following statements:
1. India ranked second globally, after China, for children with high BMI, at about 41 million.
2. The Atlas is published by the World Health Organization.
3. It was released on World Obesity Day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: It is published by the World Obesity Federation. Globally 20.7 per cent of children aged 5-19 are overweight or obese.

questions.q:
The CDSCO prohibited pharmaceutical companies from advertising GLP-1 drugs.
Statement-I: CDSCO barred advertising of GLP-1 drugs amid concerns of misuse.
Statement-II: GLP-1 receptor agonists such as Ozempic and Wegovy mimic the natural GLP-1 hormone, slow digestion and increase fullness.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The pharmacology is accurate but explains how the drugs work, not why advertising was barred. Misuse for weight loss drove the ban.

questions.q:
Data centre capacity in India rose from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,500 MW by 2025. Consider the following statements:
1. Budget 2026-27 offers a tax holiday till 2047 for eligible foreign companies providing cloud services from Indian data centres.
2. Data centres with an IT load above 5 MW got infrastructure status in 2022.
3. Cooling a 100 MW hyperscale facility needs only about 2 lakh litres of water a day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A 100 MW hyperscale facility can use up to 2 million litres daily, ten times the figure in statement 3, stressing cities such as Chennai and Bengaluru.

questions.q:
A Parliamentary Standing Committee reviewed the IndiaAI Mission. Consider the following statements:
1. The Mission used only 32 per cent of its Revised Estimate in FY2025-26 (as of December 2025).
2. As a result, the 2026-27 Budget Estimate was halved against requirements.
3. The committee found that AI research funding is spread widely across all colleges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The committee found research funding concentrated in premier institutions such as IITs and national laboratories.

questions.q:
IISc and the Pratiksha Trust launched the 'Moonshot Project' on brain co-processors. Consider the following statements:
1. Brain co-processors are AI-powered bidirectional neural interfaces that decode, analyse and re-encode brain signals.
2. A primary goal is to restore reach and grasp in stroke survivors.
3. TMS and tDCS need electrodes surgically implanted in the brain.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: TMS and tDCS are non-invasive brain stimulation techniques and need no implanted electrodes.

questions.q:
DHRUV64 has been in the news as an Indian technology milestone. Consider the following statements:
1. It is a fully indigenous 64-bit microprocessor developed by C-DAC.
2. It is meant for applications such as 5G, IoT and industrial automation.
3. It was developed by the Semiconductor Laboratory of ISRO at Chandigarh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DHRUV64 was developed by C-DAC, not by ISRO's Semiconductor Laboratory, so statement 3 is wrong. It sits in India's drive for native processors under the Microprocessor Development Programme and the Digital India RISC-V programme, which also yielded SHAKTI and VIKRAM.

questions.q:
Dual-use technologies are in focus as AI, biotechnology and space systems blur the line between civilian and military use. Consider the following statements:
1. Dual-use technologies have legitimate civilian uses but can also serve military or malicious ends.
2. India has been a member of the Wassenaar Arrangement since 2017.
3. India's SCOMET list is maintained by the Ministry of Defence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The SCOMET list of controlled items is notified by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade under the Commerce Ministry, not the Ministry of Defence, so statement 3 is wrong. India joined the Wassenaar Arrangement, an export-control regime for conventional arms and dual-use goods, in December 2017.

questions.q:
A fatal electric vehicle fire in Indore revived concern over lithium-ion battery safety. Consider the following statements:
1. A Battery Management System regulates the temperature, voltage and charging cycles of an EV battery.
2. In thermal runaway, one overheating cell can trigger a chain reaction in neighbouring cells.
3. EV battery fires burn at lower temperatures and are easier to extinguish than conventional vehicle fires.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: EV battery fires burn at higher temperatures, spread faster and are harder to put out, because they can release oxygen internally, so statement 3 is wrong. The Indore incident was worsened by LPG cylinders nearby and failed electronic door locks.
questions.h: EV battery fires are harder to put out.

questions.q:
NIOT successfully tested a Floating LiDAR Buoy System off Muttom, Tamil Nadu. Consider the following statements:
1. It measures offshore wind conditions up to 300 metres above sea level.
2. It uses laser pulses from a floating buoy.
3. NIOT functions under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NIOT, Chennai works under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

questions.q:
India is establishing a first-of-its-kind integrated Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) plant at Kavaratti, Lakshadweep. Consider the following statements:
1. OTEC generates electricity from the temperature difference between warm surface water and cold deep water.
2. It needs about a 20 degrees Celsius difference and is viable mainly in tropical oceans.
3. An OTEC plant can generate power only during daylight hours.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: OTEC runs on the temperature gap between warm surface water and cold deep water, which is steady, so it can give round-the-clock power and desalination; statement 3 is wrong. It suits the tropics (30 degrees N to 30 degrees S).

questions.q: Scientists reported 'dark oxygen' production nearly 4,000 m deep in the Pacific Ocean. It is oxygen produced
o: by hydrothermal vents splitting carbon dioxide
without sunlight, linked to electrochemical reactions involving polymetallic nodules
questions.e: It challenges the view that photosynthesis is the only major natural source of oxygen.

questions.q:
CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory has developed a production technology for dimethyl ether (DME). Consider the following statements:
1. DME is seen as a second-generation fuel that can substitute for LPG.
2. It can be blended with LPG up to about 20 per cent.
3. It can be produced only from imported crude oil.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DME can be made from Indian coal, methanol or captured CO2, so statement 3 is wrong. It burns cleanly with minimal SOx, NOx, soot and particulates, and its calorific value and thermal efficiency are comparable to conventional fuels.
